observation.visible_scene: A dance studio with a full-height mirror wall on the left, yellow walls, sheer-curtained windows and ballet barres on the right, and a potted plant. A woman with her hair in a bun, wearing a mauve long-sleeve top and dark wide-leg trousers, stands in profile facing left, holding a small white pom/flower prop at her hip. A mirror image of her appears on the left; it is a reflection, not a second person. The camera and background elements (barres, plant, window frames, mirror seams) remain fixed throughout.
visible_changes: The dancer repeatedly extends her front leg in a slow, controlled motion: in the early frames the front foot is placed forward (heel down, then flat) while the back foot supports her; around frames 12-20 the front leg lifts into a fully pointed forward extension held off the floor, then lowers back to the ground by frame 23.
After a brief grounded interval (frames 23-32), the front leg again rises into a pointed forward extension (frames 33-41), which is still held at the last frame.
The supporting (back) leg stays on the floor throughout; the torso leans slightly and the head tilts in coordination with the leg movement.
The white prop in her hand sways slightly with the body but remains in her hand; the mirror reflection reproduces the same leg and torso changes.
No camera movement is evident; all apparent motion is the dancer's own.
outside_clip_unknowns: What precedes the first frame (how the front foot reached its initial placed position) and what follows the last frame (whether the held extension is lowered, turned into a step, or repeated) are not shown.
The purpose or name of the exercise and any music/tempo cues are not visible.
uncertain_details: The exact identity of the hand-held object (flower vs. pom-pom prop) is unclear.
Which anatomical leg is the 'front' leg is hard to confirm from the profile view, so it is described by its position in the frame.
The precise quality of the movement (tendu vs. slow hold) cannot be definitively classified from sampled frames.
